newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen comfortable with Q4 estimates.
newsitem.headline: Loewen comfortable with Q4 estimates.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc said Thursday it was comfortable with analysts' earnings per share forecasts for the fourth quarter of US$0.42, excluding special costs it might incur to fight a hostile bid by
"We're comfortable with the consensus that is out there," Loewen chief financial officer Paul Wagler said in an interview.
The funeral home operator has rejected a US$2.9 billion bid by rival Service Corp International.
Loewen reported earnings from operations of US$0.29 a share in the third quarter, up from US$0.23 a year ago.
After non-recurring costs, net earnings were US$0.25 a share, up from US$0.20.
In the 1996 period those costs covered its fight against the Service Corp bid. Loewen put the total expense at US$2.6 million.
Because the Service bid was only announced in mid-September, Wagler said most of the amount was a provision for expenses anticipated at the end of the quarter but not yet incurred.
Wagler said it was impossible forecast fourth-quarter costs related to the hostile takeover bid although "it is reasonable to say there will be some expenses in the fourth quarter."
The precise amount "totally hinges on what SCI does....All I can say is that if this (bid) goes away that number will drop to a very small amount," he said.
But if the battle drags on Loewen may again in the fourth quarter have to take a provision for any foreseeable costs and bid expenses from the fourth quarter that were not covered by the provision.

Despite a drop in Loewen's share price after the third-quarter earnings announcement, Wagler said the company was pleased with its results, especially earnings from operations. "We think it was a very strong quarter," he said.

"The big story is that this is our first quarter back at 25 percent EPS gain," he said. Loewen stumbled from its historical growth rate after a lawsuit in Mississippi last year that, along with a settlement in another case, reduced its 1995 fourth-quarter earnings by US$165 million.
"We picked up a lot of (earnings) drag from Mississippi," Wagler said.
Loewen stock dropped 0.50 to 52 in Toronto and 1/8 to 39-3/8 in New York. "The earnings seemed mildly disappointing, a little light," one trader said.
Analysts on average had forecast US$0.30 a share, estimate service IBES reported earlier this week, although Wagler said the average was later reduced to US$0.29.
Bid costs had been expected to trim that number by a cent or two but the four cents a share that Loewen reported appeared to exceed expectations.
